author_or_org: Sreeja Thummala, Sophie Zeng, Mark Harman, Weini Liu, Eric Liu (Engineering at Meta)

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Meta uses a human-on-the-loop model for JiTTests: engineers set criteria and review aggregate outcomes rather than supervising every output.
claims.quote: Rather than a human-in-the-loop approach, where a human engineer reviews every output, we’ve reduced friction through a human-on-the-loop approach, where human engineers set criteria and review outcomes at an aggregate level rather than supervising every output.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Catching JiTTests focuses test generation on diffs most likely to contain severe regressions.
claims.quote: This helps ensure test generation is focused on diffs that are most likely to contain severe regressions.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: False positives are filtered with a rule-based approach plus an LLM-as-Judge ensemble that classifies weak catches as likely true or false positives.
claims.quote: To filter false positives, we employed a traditional rule-based approach combined with an ensemble approach we call “LLM-as-Judge,” which aggregates judgements from several state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs, all tasked with classifying weak catches as likely true or false positives.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The system uses the ranking from LLM-as-Judge and RubFake to decide whether to bring in a human engineer.
claims.quote: Based on the ranking from LLM-as-Judge and RubFake, the system then decides whether to reach out to human engineers.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: As of the article, 589 Meta engineers had engaged with Catching JiTTests, representing 64% of outreach, and the reported true-positive rate was 60%.
claims.quote: As of this writing, 589 engineers at Meta (64% of our outreach) have engaged with Catching JiTTests. These engineers have reported that Catching JiTTests surfaces genuinely actionable findings, with a 60% rate of true positives.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: In the first half of 2026, Catching JiTTests caught 74 serious privacy bugs at the diff stage and lowered overall privacy SEVs by 20%.
claims.quote: In the first half of 2026, Catching JiTTests played a key role in catching 74 serious (SEV) privacy bugs at the diff stage, before they landed in production and lowering the overall occurrence of privacy SEVs by 20% during that timeframe.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Catching JiTTests generates executable tests that demonstrate a concrete behavioral difference and can catch bug classes that LLM- or agent-based code review might miss, at the cost of more computational steps.
claims.quote: It generates executable tests that demonstrate a concrete behavioral difference introduced by the change. While it requires more computational steps, it catches classes of bugs that LLM- or agent-based code reviews might not.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Meta describes the approach as generalizable: engineers define success criteria early, AI executes testing, engineers monitor aggregate outcomes, and intervention happens at the policy level rather than per item.
claims.quote: The approach is generalizable: Engineers define success criteria early, let AI execute the testing, monitor the outcomes at an aggregate level, and intervene at the policy level rather than per item.
